title: Choose Agent Moshpit's visual world
question: The roll assigned Do Not Disturb. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Do Not Disturb
options.thesis: Every agent is a door, and its hanger tells you whether to knock.
options.viewport: A corridor of doors, one row per agent, hanger at the handle; anyone saying PLEASE KNOCK moves to the top.
options.risk: A hanger holds two or three words, and the classic red-for-keep-out is given up so the loudest colour means 'needs you'.

raised.raise: Every hanger, row and gap snaps to one visible module.
Only hangers carry saturated colour; the rest of the shell stays on one petrol scale.
Each state also has its own printed mark, so no status depends on colour alone.
When someone needs you, that zone owns the top of the window as one flat colour field.
A working agent shows a strip of its real recent tool calls, one bar per call, instead of a spinner.

regions.label: doors: agent, what it is doing

options.label: The In/Out Board
options.lineage: office staff in/out boards with sliding pegs
options.thesis: One board, four columns, a peg per agent: read down a column to see who needs you.
options.viewport: Names down the left; WORKING, NEEDS YOU, DONE and IDLE across the top; one peg sliding along each row.
options.risk: The most familiar of the hand: close to a status table, the least playful, and tight in a narrow window.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and airport gate boards
options.thesis: Agents are flights: the board reranks by urgency, and a changed row stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: A fixed-column board, most urgent first; opening an agent shows its boarding pass: task, repository, branch, model, elapsed.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and equals the hangers on clarity, and travel suits the name. It is an airport, not an office, so it loses on the brief's own picture.
options.risk: Reads as a status display for flights rather than a place where colleagues work.

regions.label: boarding pass of the selected agent

options.label: Gardens Guide Map
options.thesis: Each workspace is a swelling lobe of flat colour with its agents standing on it.
options.viewport: One green headland per repository, agents as markers on its coast, capsule controls in yellow and coral.
options.case: The most playful of the hand, but one lobe per screen hides the other agents, and overshooting motion fights a status strip read in peripheral vision.
options.kept: Colour committed at region scale, not sprinkled as accents.
options.risk: A map shows where things are, not who needs you.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Two short columns around a rail of keys, with notes bracketed in the margin.
options.viewport: Agents set as reference entries; a waiting question hangs in the margin, bracketed to its line.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish rather than an office, and small roman columns cannot be read in a sideways glance.
options.kept: A full vocabulary of printed marks for state, so nothing depends on colour.
options.risk: Reads as a document, not a workplace.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Status words assembled cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid-built status words over a small grotesk list of agents.
options.case: Fuses poorly: specimen-scale letterforms fight a dense agent list and a narrow window.
options.kept: A strict visible module that every element snaps to.
options.risk: Legibility drops fast at small sizes.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Agents as barcode columns in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars, one column per agent, numbers packed in the margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: cold rather than a place to enjoy, bars cannot be read as status, and strobing is hostile in peripheral vision.
options.kept: Activity drawn from real data: a strip of actual tool calls, not a spinner.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white with a single accent used sparingly.
options.viewport: A quiet list of agents in one neutral scale with one accent.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a claim-and-proof marketing form has no shape for a live floor, and one accent cannot separate four states.
options.kept: Colour restraint: saturated colour appears only where it carries status.

canonCard.label: The category standard: pixel office
canonCard.thesis: A top-down pixel-art room with an animated character at every desk.
canonCard.viewport: The whole room in one view; a speech bubble appears over an agent that needs you.
canonCard.risk: Hermes Pixel Office and Agent Office already ship this for Hermes; Agent Moshpit would differ only by being a native app you can act from.
